findings.quote: NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES
findings.rationale: Section 15.11 excludes indirect damages mutually but there is no aggregate liability cap anywhere in the Agreement, so both parties (including us) are exposed without limit; our playbook requires at least a mutual cap with carve-outs. We have added a mutual cap that expressly leaves our Article 6 payment obligations and the usual Excluded Claims outside it.

replacement.oldText: FOR THE AVOIDANCE OF DOUBT, THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2.
replacement.newText: FOR THE AVOIDANCE OF DOUBT, THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2. EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS AND PB'S PAYMENT OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE 6 AND SECTION 14.2, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR DAMAGES ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE DEVELOPMENT COSTS ACTUALLY PAID OR INCURRED BY SFJ HEREUNDER AND (B) ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS ($1,000,000). "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OR DATA PROTECTION OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] Our position is a mutual aggregate cap with uncapped carve-outs for indemnities, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. We have kept our Article 6 and Section 14.2 payment obligations outside the cap so the economics are unaffected.

findings.quote: (f) actual or alleged infringement of any Third Party's Intellectual Property by the Product or by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder with respect to the Product
findings.rationale: SFJ's indemnity (12.1.1) covers its gross negligence and breaches but excludes IP infringement, while we indemnify SFJ for third-party IP claims arising from either Party's performance — the reverse of our position that the vendor carries IP risk for its own activities. We have narrowed our indemnity to our own conduct and put SFJ's activities back on SFJ.

replacement.oldText: (f) actual or alleged infringement of any Third Party's Intellectual Property by the Product or by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder with respect to the Product
replacement.newText: (f) actual or alleged infringement of any Third Party's Intellectual Property by the Product or by PB in performing its duties or obligations hereunder with respect to the Product (excluding any such infringement to the extent arising from the activities, materials, methods or technology of SFJ, its Affiliates or its Permitted Third Parties, for which SFJ shall defend and indemnify the PB Indemnified Parties)
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We accept IP risk in the Product itself, but not for infringement caused by SFJ's own conduct or technology; each party should carry the IP risk it creates.

findings.quote: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
findings.rationale: Our only convenience right is gated on SFJ having funded $60M and on the pre-approval period, while SFJ has several unilateral exit rights (Material Adverse Event, change of control, JSC disagreement); our playbook requires an unconditional Customer exit on notice. We have removed the gating conditions and set a 60-day notice period.

replacement.oldText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
replacement.newText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to SFJ.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We need an unconditional right to terminate for convenience on notice (30 days preferred, 60 days as fallback), not one gated on a funding threshold and the pre-approval window.

findings.quote: an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination
findings.rationale: Termination triggers fixed multiples payable by us — 300% of Development Costs (14.2.1, 14.2.2, 14.2.5.2, 14.2.7), 150% on a change of control or compliance breach, and Development Costs plus 25% interest under 14.2.10 — all on top of continuing Approval Payments; these are liquidated damages far beyond our 3-months'-fees fallback. We have reduced the convenience-termination multiple to a return of funding.

replacement.oldText: PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
replacement.newText: PB will pay SFJ, within ninety (90) days of the date of termination, an amount equal to one hundred percent (100%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept liquidated damages against us; because we also remain liable for Approval Payments, a repayment of SFJ's actual funding is the appropriate exit amount. The 150% and 25%-interest formulas elsewhere in Section 14.2 should be conformed.

findings.quote: SFJ may, in its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement in its entirety at any time following a Change of Control of PB that occurs prior to the date of payment by PB of the final Approval Payment.
findings.rationale: Section 15.6 sensibly permits assignment to affiliates and successors, but Section 14.2.6 lets SFJ terminate on our change of control and charge 150% of Development Costs, which is walk-away territory for us. We have removed the change-of-control termination right where the successor assumes our obligations.

replacement.oldText: SFJ may, in its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement in its entirety at any time following a Change of Control of PB that occurs prior to the date of payment by PB of the final Approval Payment.
replacement.newText: SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement, and no additional payment shall become due from PB, solely by reason of a Change of Control of PB, provided that the successor assumes PB's obligations under this Agreement.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] A vendor termination or re-pricing right triggered by our change of control is not acceptable; assumption of obligations by the successor protects SFJ's economics.

findings.quote: SFJ hereby represents, warrants and covenants that it will have, as and when needed, sufficient funds to satisfy its obligations hereunder.
findings.rationale: SFJ gives only corporate, funding and compliance representations, with no warranty that the SFJ Services will be performed to a professional standard and no remedy, and Section 13.6.2 disclaims everything else. We have inserted a short performance warranty with a re-performance remedy.

replacement.oldText: SFJ hereby represents, warrants and covenants that it will have, as and when needed, sufficient funds to satisfy its obligations hereunder.
replacement.newText: SFJ hereby represents, warrants and covenants that it will have, as and when needed, sufficient funds to satisfy its obligations hereunder. SFJ further warrants that the SFJ Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by suitably qualified personnel and in accordance with the Protocols, GCP and all Applicable Laws, and that SFJ will promptly re-perform, at its own cost and not as a Development Cost, any SFJ Services that fail to conform to this warranty.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We expect an express services warranty with a re-performance remedy; "Commercially Reasonable Efforts" alone leaves us without recourse for defective trial execution.

findings.quote: SFJ shall be the sole and exclusive owner of the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein.
findings.rationale: We retain ownership of all Existing PB Intellectual Property and Trial Inventions and buy back the Trial Data Package on the earlier of approval or termination, so ownership ends with us; however SFJ takes a first-priority security interest over all of our IP (7.1), can force a Program Transfer of the whole programme on specified defaults (3.20), and can gate our out-licensing (7.5.5). These are financing features rather than IP drafting points and need business/finance sign-off rather than a redline.

findings.quote: effective as of such termination, SFJ shall, and it hereby does, assign to PB all of SFJ's and its Affiliates' right, title and interest in and to all Product Filings then owned or Controlled by SFJ or any of its Affiliates
findings.rationale: Section 14.3 gives us assignment of the Trial Data Package and Product Filings, delivery of all data, transfer or wind-down of ongoing trials and assignment of CRO/site agreements — better than our preferred exit package.

findings.quote: each Party will maintain the following types of insurance coverage at a minimum level
findings.rationale: Section 12.3 requires commercial general, umbrella, clinical trial and professional liability cover with A- rated insurers, certificates on request and additional-insured status for us; the limits are redacted and should be confirmed against our thresholds.

findings.quote: will be governed by the internal laws of the State of Delaware, USA
findings.rationale: Delaware law sits at our accepted fallback and the arbitration is seated in New York under ICDR rules, so no foreign seat; we note only that we would prefer courts to mandatory arbitration.

findings.quote: During the Term and for a period of [***] thereafter, neither Party shall solicit an employee of the other Party who is or has been involved in the performance or oversight of any of the development activities hereunder
findings.rationale: The non-solicit is mutual, limited to personnel involved in the programme, contains a general-advertising carve-out and includes no no-hire, which meets our fallback; we should confirm the redacted tail period is no more than 12 months.

findings.quote: During the applicable Exclusive Period, SFJ shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, either by itself or through a Third Party, conduct human clinical trials of, or sell, offer for sale or have sold:
findings.rationale: The only exclusivity runs against SFJ and in our favour, so there is nothing to redline under this rule.

findings.quote: PB shall not, without SFJ's prior written consent, enter into a Licensing Transaction unless such Licensing Transaction is an Excluded Licensing Transaction
findings.rationale: No field-of-use or non-compete restriction binds us; the only competitive restraint (Section 3.19) binds SFJ. We note the Section 7.5.5 consent gate on Licensing Transactions as a financing covenant (mitigated by the Excluded Licensing Transaction carve-outs and expedited arbitration), which we have raised under the IP/security package review.
We found no most-favoured-nation, best-terms or price-matching obligation binding us anywhere in the Agreement.

findings.quote: PB shall spend at least an amount equal to the amount of funding paid by SFJ to PB pursuant to this Section 4.2.
findings.rationale: There is no take-or-pay or volume commitment; we control the Elected Total Amount ($110–120M) and the spend covenant simply requires funding to be applied to the programme.

findings.quote: PB shall (a) provide SFJ with quarterly unaudited financial statements and annual audited financial statements
findings.rationale: There is no usage-verification or audit right allowing SFJ into our systems; the information rights are periodic financial reporting and mutual quality-audit reports, which we accept.

findings.quote: All rights not exclusively granted to SFJ are reserved to PB and its Affiliates.
findings.rationale: No licence is granted to us because we retain ownership of the Product IP, so the licence-scope rule is not engaged.

findings.quote: The term of this Agreement (the "Term") will commence on the Effective Date and will expire upon the earliest of (i) termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 14.2
findings.rationale: The Term runs to the final Approval Payment with no automatic renewal, notice window or price-uplift mechanic, so there is nothing to shorten or cap.
